name: Video Reflection Consistency
description: Detects inconsistencies in reflections on surfaces and eyes across video frames.
useCase: Identifying deepfakes through reflection anomalies in eyes, glasses, and reflective surfaces
mechanism: Analyzes specular highlights and reflections in eyes, glasses, and other reflective surfaces for consistency with the environment. AI-generated videos frequently produce incorrect corneal reflections, mismatched specular highlights, or physically impossible reflection patterns.
source: Hu, S. et al. (2021) - Exposing GAN-generated Faces Using Inconsistent Corneal Specular Highlights, ICASSP
algorithm: Corneal Reflection Detection + Specular Highlight Tracking + Cross-Frame Consistency
parameters: Eye detection: landmark-based, Reflection extraction: thresholding + clustering, Consistency: correlation
strengths:
• Very specific artifact unique to deepfakes
• Corneal reflections are hard for AI to fake
• Works on close-up face videos
• High precision when reflections are visible
limitations:
• Requires visible eye reflections
• Glasses can obscure corneal reflections
• Low resolution reduces effectiveness
• Dark scenes may lack sufficient reflections

references.title: Hu, S. et al. (2021). Exposing GAN-generated Faces Using Inconsistent Corneal Specular Highlights. ICASSP.
Guo, X. et al. (2022). Eyes Tell All: Detecting Political Orientation from Eye Movement Data. AAAI.
Matern, F. et al. (2019). Exploiting Visual Artifacts to Expose Deepfakes. WACV.
